problem.title: Four Tokens in a Row
problem.statement: Red, Blue, Green, and Yellow tokens occupy positions 1 through 4, one token per position. Red is immediately left of Blue. Green is not in position 1 or 4. Yellow is left of Green. Which token is in position 1?
hints: Try the Red-Blue block in positions 1-2, 2-3, and 3-4.
Apply both Green's restriction and Yellow's left-of clue to each block position.

solutionSteps.title: Test the block
solutionSteps.body: Red-Blue in 1-2 leaves positions 3-4 for Green and Yellow, but Green must be 3 and then Yellow cannot be left of Green. Red-Blue in 2-3 leaves only endpoints for Green, which is forbidden.

solutionSteps.title: Use the survivor
solutionSteps.body: Red-Blue must be in 3-4. Green then occupies position 2 and Yellow occupies position 1. The unique order is Yellow, Green, Red, Blue.

validationMethods: exhaustive test of the three possible Red-Blue block positions
independent enumeration of all 24 token permutations
notes: Exactly one permutation satisfies all three clues: Yellow, Green, Red, Blue.

problem.title: The Middle Gem
problem.statement: Ruby is heavier than Emerald. Emerald is heavier than Sapphire. Which gem has the middle weight?
hints: Write both comparisons with the heavier gem on the left.
Connect the two comparisons through Emerald.

solutionSteps.title: Join the clues
solutionSteps.body: The comparisons form Ruby > Emerald > Sapphire, so Emerald is between the other two weights.

validationMethods: transitive ordering Ruby greater than Emerald greater than Sapphire
independent audit of all six strict rankings
notes: Emerald is uniquely the middle gem.

problem.title: The Third Book
problem.statement: Books A, B, and C are placed in positions 1 through 3, one book per position. A is somewhere before B, and C is not in position 3. Which book must be in position 3?
hints: List the orders in which A appears before B.
Remove any order ending in C.

solutionSteps.title: List survivors
solutionSteps.body: The orders with A before B are ABC, ACB, and CAB. Removing ABC because C is third leaves ACB and CAB; both place B third.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of six book orders
independent case split on C in position 1 or 2
notes: Two full orders survive, but both force B into position 3.

problem.title: Exactly One Door Sign
problem.statement: A prize is behind exactly one of doors A, B, and C. Three signs say: I. The prize is behind A. II. The prize is not behind B. III. The prize is not behind A. Exactly one sign is true. Which door hides the prize?
hints: Assume each door in turn and count true signs.
The required truth count is exactly one.

solutionSteps.title: Count each row
solutionSteps.body: Prize at A makes signs I and II true. Prize at B makes only sign III true. Prize at C makes signs II and III true.

solutionSteps.title: Keep the required row
solutionSteps.body: Only Door B has exactly one true sign.

validationMethods: complete three-row truth table with counts 2, 1, and 2
independent direct substitution of each prize location
notes: Door B is the unique location producing exactly one true sign.

problem.title: Four Workshop Days
problem.statement: Workshops J, K, L, and M are scheduled on days 1 through 4, one per day. J is before K. L is immediately after K. M is on day 1. On which day is K?
hints: Fit the consecutive K-L block while leaving an earlier position for J.

solutionSteps.title: Fit the block
solutionSteps.body: With M on day 1, K-L cannot be days 2-3 because J would have no open earlier day. Therefore K-L is days 3-4 and J is day 2.

validationMethods: case audit of the possible consecutive K-L positions
independent enumeration of all 24 workshop schedules
notes: The unique schedule is M, J, K, L, so K is on day 3.

problem.title: Exactly Two Suspect Statements
problem.statement: Exactly one of Ava, Bo, and Celine caused a spill. Ava says, “Bo did it.” Bo says, “Celine did it.” Celine says, “Bo is innocent.” Exactly two statements are true. Who caused the spill?
hints: Assume each person is the culprit in turn.
Count all three statements under each assumption.

solutionSteps.title: Test Ava and Bo
solutionSteps.body: If Ava did it, only Celine's statement is true. If Bo did it, only Ava's statement is true.

solutionSteps.title: Test Celine
solutionSteps.body: If Celine did it, Bo's statement and Celine's statement are true while Ava's is false. This gives exactly two truths.

validationMethods: complete culprit truth table with truth counts 1, 1, and 2
independent semantic evaluation of each quoted claim
notes: Celine is the unique culprit producing exactly two true statements.
